reading: The Lit Manual line has been near the top of every round it entered: 8.02, 8.01 and 7.56 on the tour, 7.73 on the landing panel, and 7.64 for x14a-manual-cross, Slotted. That score was +0.27 on its carried design and +0.19 on Joined. The judges consistently like five things about it. It is the best-set type in the field: a one-line Plex Sans Condensed title with the lit word and its full stop last, mono date and time columns on the rail, and a small-caps figure row. Its system is calm (system 8: "the calmest and most typographic system", hairline rules instead of boxes). The rail with one lit NOW runs everywhere, Settings now included. It has the most varied colour in its heat (hue entropy .58). And the Status wiring figure, the head figures and the colophon lamp all earn their place. Three things sank it. (1) The four-week slot glass that replaced the round countdown. Every lens called it a tall, half-empty equaliser with 10px numerals and an unnamed "Next in 2 days", and lessons.md lists it as a failed reach. The fix is to shrink it or to put content on it, never to stretch it. The tour judges had loved the round countdown tube (soul: "the most beautiful new tubes"), and Desk then took that same dial and gave its lit ticks day numerals ("a proper 1980s instrument"). (2) Below the welcome plate, Home goes flat and unlit (soul, style, skeptic: "give each section one lamp"). (3) Ideas lost its radar emphasis and starts its list low, the Plans NOW trace is easy to miss, Settings' two columns share row heights, the form leaves a dead right column, and the Remind me starter looks selected at rest. A win needs four things. Go back to the round tube, carrying real data and the plan's name. Wire that lit object to its own list with one short straight line, which is the grammar behind every graft that took this round. Give each lower section one lamp. Keep the manual's type and its varied, grounded colour. The line must also leave "Give Vera something to plan." to other lines (convergence) and try a title nobody has used.

briefs.name: Lit Manual, Dialled
briefs.hypothesis: Slotted lost points on exactly one object, the slot glass, and gained on everything else. Putting the line's own round countdown tube back fixes the failed reach. Desk's day-numeral ticks give the tube real data (the four plan days, plus the free weekend as a sage arc), and a printed caption names the plan. A short leader line, as in a technical manual's callout, joins the tube to Coming up's NOW lamp. This is the 'light wired to what it reports' grammar that won heat a. Plate's engraved day numeral then becomes the one mark shared by the dial's ticks, the rail's stops and the month's cells. So the figure finally touches its rows, which is this line's founding rule. Each lower section also gets one lamp, which answers the 'flat below the fold' fault that held the line under 8. Nothing that scored is lost: the type, the hairline system, the rails, the colophon, the Status wiring, the 0.58 hue entropy.
briefs.brief:
Start from x14a-manual-cross (x14b-a/palettes/x14a-manual-cross.json, x14b-a/variants/x14a-manual-cross/: sheet.css, templates/_ui.html, home.html, plans.html, plans_month.html, ideas.html, idea_form.html, settings.html, settings_section.html, tasks.html, status.html, _machine.html, _anatomy.html). Keep the palette tokens: green-black ground, bone ink, drawing-ink rails, amber for late and due, sage for free, slate-blue plates, #6dff9c only where the phosphor is. Keep the Plex superfamily and its jobs: Sans Condensed for heads, Sans for text, Mono for times, VT323 only inside tubes.

HOME (home.html):
1. Welcome plate, left: keep the layout, the one-line title (new words, see title), the full-width box and the three starters. Fix: the 'Remind me to…' starter must match its siblings at rest. Find what latches it in the still (a :focus-visible, :target or .is-on rule on .starters a; check `.starters a:nth-child(2)` and any `[aria-current]`) and drop it. The hover and focus states stay the same for all three.
2. Under the box, replace the plain glance strip (3 / 4 / 3) with a LEADERED READOUT row (see graft 3). Cells, in order: NEXT ··· Sun **4** (the day numeral lit phosphor, linked to the plan), PLANS ··· 4, TO DO ··· 4, LATE ··· 3 (amber numeral and label), IDEAS ··· 12. Labels are caps eyebrows at 0.75rem, +0.06em tracking, bone-dim. Leaders are 1px dotted drawing-ink. Numerals are Plex Mono tabular, 1.5rem, weight 500, bone (LATE amber, NEXT's day phosphor with the E1 halo). Every cell is a link with a 44px tall target. On the phone the row wraps 2+3 and NEXT comes first, so the next plan is above the fold.
3. Figure, right: DELETE the slot glass (.slot-tube, .slot-plot, .slot-axis, .slot-now, .slot-head, .slot-foot, .slot-name, .slot-cap and their markup). Put back the round countdown tube as a shared macro `dial(next, plans, window=28, size='lg'|'sm')` in _ui.html, built from the line's own .dial/.dial-case/.dial-ring/.dial-big and taking Desk's tick geometry (graft 1). The face is VT323: 'NEXT IN' small, the big numeral '2' at 3.5rem with the E1 two-layer halo and a hot core, 'DAYS' small. Around the bezel run 28 day ticks (week ticks longer). Plan days get a lit blip, the next one white-hot, and their DAY NUMERAL (4, 9, 17, 24) is set upright inside the ring at 1rem minimum (the type lens asked for 1.25rem on the next). The first free weekend (10-11 Oct) is a 2-day SAGE arc on the bezel (token --sage, no glow, 3px stroke) with a tiny sage 'free' label, which keeps the slot glass's sage free-weekend data. Size: 15rem on desktop, the glass at or under 14rem high, scanlines and a third of a pixel of blur, the case's power lamp lit (kit E12). Under the case goes a caption in manual style, no 'Fig.' prefix: '**Oaks Park roller rink** · Sun 4 Oct, 13:00 · then 3 more · 10 Oct free', in Plex Sans 0.875rem bone, the plan name weight 600. This names the plan (usability) and fills the space the glass left empty.
4. Swap the two lower columns: Coming up goes into the RIGHT column, directly under the dial, and To do moves left. Align the dial's foot over Coming up's rail x (the rail runs at the column's left edge plus about 108px; set the dial's left edge so its centre is on that x, or move the rail under the dial's centre). A LEADER (graft 2) drops straight down from the case's bottom socket to Coming up's NOW lamp: 2px, phosphor at full strength with a 4px bloom, about 60-90px long, no turns. It tapers to 1px at 40% past NOW along the rail's first segment and stops at the next stop. Nothing else on Home is wired. On the phone the dial sits after the readout row at 11rem, centred, with the same short drop into Coming up.
5. Coming up's rail: the stops lose their 1-4 ring numbers. Each stop leads with the ENGRAVED DAY NUMERAL (graft 3b): Plex Sans Condensed 300 at 1.75rem, tabular, tracking -0.02em, with the month and weekday stacked beside it in 0.7rem caps. The next plan's numeral is phosphor with the E1 halo, the others bone. It is the same numeral the dial's tick shows, which is the one mark joining figure and list. Time stays mono, and 'in 2 days' stays bone-dim.
6. To do (left): keep the amber due words and the left amber rule on late rows. Keep its NOW rule (the left half-rail with 'NOW') at full phosphor for the lamp only. Due dates lead with the same day numeral in bone at 1.5rem.
7. Lower half, one lamp per section (soul, skeptic): Finish setting up keeps its numbered rail, with the next step's ring lit (a phosphor lamp, 8px core and halo) and the others drawing-ink. The kids' wishes gets a small sage lamp per kid with an open wish, or a dim ring for 'nothing open', and the line 'Maya, Theo · nothing open' at 0.875rem. Lately added becomes a rail too: newest first, the newest row's stop a small lamp, kind as a 6px square in its kind colour (keep those hues, they carry the entropy). Cap Finish setting up and Lately added at a 46rem measure (type), and use the spare width for the wishes column, so nothing runs edge to edge.
8. Keep the colophon with its breathing lamp at the foot of every page.

PLANS (plans.html, plans_month.html): use the shared `dial(size='sm')` at 13rem, with the same day numerals on its ticks and the same sage free arc. Keep the caption ('Next: Oaks Park roller rink, Sun 4 Oct 13:00, then 3 more.'), and drop the 'FIG. 1' prefix. Month cells: a plan day's date numeral uses the engraved style, bone weight 500. The next plan's day is phosphor with the halo, and the free weekend's cells get a sage 1px top rule and a 4% sage tint. The month NOW trace goes to 2px at 50% phosphor, with a lamp at both ends (system, interaction, feedback). Cut the 90px of quiet space beside the dial by starting the grid level with the dial's top. In the list view, rows lead with the engraved numeral, as on Home.

IDEAS (ideas.html): move the radar into the head row at the right (page_head figure slot), at the parent's tour size (about 15rem case). Set Nearest and Furthest as two leadered readout lines beside it, the same component as Home's readout. The list's filters and kind chips then start directly under the head, so the first rows are above the 900px fold. Remove the radar's own block. Blips keep their phosphor; links in Nearest and Furthest are bone with an underline on hover only.

TO DO (tasks.html): keep the Late filter tab, the NOW rail and the amber due words. Dates lead with the engraved numeral (bone, amber when late). Keep the counter figure only if it shows what the list cannot (deadlines against NOW). Otherwise put the filters in its place (interaction).

SETTINGS (settings.html, settings_section.html, templates/settings/): the two-column railed parts become TWO independent lists (`.settings-cols > ol.railed` twice, the parts split left and right by order), so each row takes its own height and AI model loses its gap. Every form label on every page (the settings sections, the idea form, family, login) gets ONE rule, `.field > label, legend`: Plex Sans 600, 0.75rem, uppercase, +0.06em tracking, bone-dim. When the field is focused, the label lights phosphor (the idea form's lit field name, made universal via `:focus-within`). Do not synthesize small caps.

IDEA FORM (idea_form.html): fill the dead right column with a manual figure at 18rem: 'Where it lands'. It shows Lately added's rail with a ghost dashed row '#13 · this idea', its kind square updating from the kind select (CSS only, :has() on the select's value where supported, static otherwise), and the kind's ring. No script.

STATUS: keep the wiring figure and its lamps. The spend gauge gets back its power light (kit E12).

PHOSPHOR KIT (phosphor_kit.md): the dial and the radar are real tubes (VT323 at three strengths, bloom, scanlines, the corners falling into shadow). The leader is the one lit line on Home. 'plan.' in the title keeps its hot core over its rising pool. Nothing else glows. Keep green at or under about 60% of saturated pixels: sage (free), amber (late), the slate-blue plates and the kind hues stay.
briefs.borrows:
OWN JUDGES' FIXES (dossier, crossing round 14a): rework the slot glass. Every lens asked for this, and style asked outright to 'go back to the round Next-in tube'. Name the next plan (usability, interaction). Raise the tube's numerals to at least 1.25rem, the next one hot (type). Restore the Ideas radar to the parent's size and bring the list above the fold (soul, feedback, interaction). Plans NOW trace at 2px, about 50%, with a lamp at both ends (feedback, system, interaction). Settings as two independent lists (system). Small-caps eyebrow as the universal form label at 0.75rem, +0.06em (system, type), done as tracked caps so it is not synthesized. Right-hand figure on the idea form (system). Cap setup and Lately added at about 46rem (type). The Remind me starter at rest (usability, skeptic). One lamp in each lower section and a live light below the fold (soul, skeptic). Restore the spend gauge's power light (designer's own weakness). Also from the landing panel: drop the 'Fig.' prefix where a caption is only a label (style, system).

GRAFTS FROM THE MAIN CAMP:
1. Day numerals on the countdown dial's lit ticks, from x14a-desk-cross Desk Terminal, Patched (ledger X14a-03, 'a proper 1980s instrument', soul). Files: x14b-a/variants/x14a-desk-cross/templates/_ui.html (the dial SVG around line 274: .dial-tick with .on/.next/.wk, .dial-blip, .dial-blip-halo, .dial-day counter-rotated text) and the .dial* rules in x14b-a/variants/x14a-desk-cross/sheet.css. Shots: x14b-a/out/x14a-desk-cross/shots/plans.png. This is Manual's own dial coming home improved. It is rebuilt here in the manual's case and bone/sage terms, with a sage free-weekend arc Desk does not have, and shared by Home and Plans as one macro.
2. The patch lead, from x14a-desk-cross (X14a-01, 'the best graft in the heat', system and style). Files: x14b-a/variants/x14a-desk-cross/templates/home.html (the Coming up block, from line ~91) and its sheet.css lead rules. It is rebuilt as the manual's callout LEADER: a straight vertical drop from the dial's socket onto NOW, tapered after NOW. Taking it this way follows the corrected form from lessons' failed reach 3 (Listing's long right-angled jog), not a cable across empty ground.
3a. The leadered readout strip, from x14a-dessau-cross Dessau, Wired Through (X14a-12, 'the best head device in the heat and should be a standard', system). Files: x14b-a/variants/x14a-dessau-cross/templates/_ui.html (macro `strip`, line 243), its home.html call and sheet.css .strip/.leader/.readout rules. It replaces Manual's own glance strip, keeping its links. The skeptic's caveat is taken: grounded ink (bone and amber), with only NEXT lit.
3b. The engraved day numeral leading every dated list, from x14a-plate-cross Plate, Engraved (X14a-20, 'should become the standard', type). Files: x14b-b/variants/x14a-plate-cross/templates/_ui.html (macro `daynum`, line 106), home.html (.plan-row .d.day, line ~114, and the dues lookup ~158-165), and the .num-fig rules in x14b-b/variants/x14a-plate-cross/sheet.css (~2019). Set in this line's Plex Sans Condensed light, not Plate's face, and tied to the dial's tick numerals.
briefs.avoids:
The slot glass as a tall, half-empty equaliser with 10px numerals and an unnamed 'Next in 2 days' (every lens in 14a; lessons' failed reach 2): the glass is removed, the round tube returns at or under 14rem of glass, with real data on its ticks and the plan named under it. 'Flat and unlit below the fold' (soul, style, skeptic): each lower section gets one lamp, and Lately added becomes a rail. Ideas' dull radar tile and low list (soul, feedback, interaction). The Plans NOW trace that can be missed. Settings' shared row heights. The bare one-column form. The Remind me starter that looks latched. Captions in tiny mono and 'Fig.' costume (type, skeptic). Convergence: the line gives up 'Give Vera something to plan.' and the numbered 1-4 rings shared with other lines, and keeps its own dial and leader rather than taking a ring setup strip. Colour drain: sage gets a new job (the free arc and cells) when the slot glass goes, so no hue is removed without a replacement. Grafts that read as pasted: the cable is a short straight leader, not a socket-and-patch costume, and the readout uses the manual's own index leaders.

WHAT IT GIVES UP to make room: the four-week slot glass and its bar plot, the 1-4 ring numbers on the rails (the day numerals take their job), the plain 3/4/3 glance strip, the Ideas radar's own block below the head, and Home's column order (Coming up moves right, under the tube).
briefs.title: Hand Vera anything to *plan.*: one line in Plex Sans Condensed bone, with the full stop inside the lit run as Manual set it (the setting system and type credited in 14a). This title has not been tried before. It is an imperative in the manual's own voice, like the line's 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (8.02 and 8.01 on the tour), which TRY NEXT now hands to Trued. It names who hears you. 'Hand' is the physical act of passing something over, the way the family passes a weekend, a reminder, an idea or a wish to the bot to plan: this is FamilyDB's job. 'Anything' is broader than 'something' and refuses nothing. The judges objected to 'Anything to plan?' as a question ('a waiter asking'); as an imperative it is not a question. It is also distinct in the field, so the line stops converging on 'Give Vera something to plan.'. The lit word comes last, where the eye stops, directly above the box it labels.
